title: Planning a Debate
text:
A debate outline is a plan that helps a speaker organize their arguments before a debate. It usually starts with a clear statement of the topic and the speaker's position. After that, the outline lists the main reasons, and under each reason the speaker writes evidence such as facts, examples, or expert opinions.

A good outline also includes possible counterarguments, which are the points the other side may raise. Writing these in advance helps the speaker prepare short and clear answers. Many students feel more confident during the debate when their outline is well made.

questions.text: What does a debate outline usually start with?
options: A list of the judges' names
A clear statement of the topic and the speaker's position
A summary of the other team's speech

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what should a good outline include?
options: Jokes to make the audience laugh

questions.text: Why do speakers write counterarguments in advance?
options: So they can finish the debate early
So they can avoid making any arguments
So they can prepare short and clear answers
So they can change their position during the debate

questions.text: What can be inferred about students who prepare a well-made outline?
options: They are likely to feel more confident
They never need to speak in debates
They have already won the debate
They do not need to collect evidence

vocabulary.definition: a plan that shows the main points of something
facts or examples that show something is true
feeling sure of yourself and your abilities

paragraph_translations: Um esboço de debate é um plano que ajuda o orador a organizar seus argumentos antes de um debate. Geralmente começa com uma declaração clara do tema e da posição do orador. Depois disso, o esboço lista as principais razões e, abaixo de cada razão, o orador escreve evidências, como fatos, exemplos ou opiniões de especialistas.

Um bom esboço também inclui possíveis contra-argumentos, que são os pontos que o outro lado pode levantar. Escrevê-los com antecedência ajuda o orador a preparar respostas curtas e claras. Muitos estudantes se sentem mais confiantes durante o debate quando o esboço é bem feito.
